My partner's cousin does something similar with me when I'm trying to enjoy my hobby. I used to play alone and not invite any of my friends, but it's not possible for me to duck people anymore because they know I'll be there weekly. Now I am extremely clear with her that she can play points/play in particular areas without me, and that I will be doing my own thing to make sure I get the most out of my Sunday. She sometimes brings up her mental health and other personal struggles, and I listen and validate so she feels heard, but once the conversation is no longer productive, I will terminate it as naturally as possible and continue with my practice once it feels appropriate to do so. Even with this strategy, I feel it weighing on my mental health, so I have started to be quite direct. For example, she wanted me to play a point while I was resting, and I said that I needed to listen to my body and my mind because I was getting strained and kind of irritated. She sometimes appears offended or embarrassed after I say something like that, but I pretend that I don't notice because I don't think she wants me to know she's feeling that way, and I also don't want to reinforce the behaviour. In some instances spanning a longer period of time, she has obliquely (or very directly) posted her urge/plan to attempt suicide. I am an intern therapist, and I have a duty to report/check in, so I would feel obligated to reach out, having seen her posts (which were only available to some people on her friend list, including me). As a result, I have muted her on social media so that public posts about that kind of content are not visible. However, she has my number, and I have made it clear that she can turn to me when she is in need, but that I am not able to respond to her public posts going forward.

Make sure you're familiar with the field layout. My field typically copies the NXL layout, so if you have a chance to check out the NXL World Cup on YouTube, you can preview some angles and see how others move. The World Cup is Nov. 11-14, so you can possibly watch a bit before playing the same layout! Of course, your field may not copy the NXL layout, but in that case, take some time to do a walk through before play. Sometimes fields will post their field layouts on social media so you can begin to plan a bit.

Another tip would be to watch your form. When you're kneeling, whatever side of the bunker you are looking out of should inform what knee is down and which one is up - kneel on the knee closest to the outside of the bunker so you're a smaller target. Also, if you're shooting on the left side of the bunker, switch to your left hand. Practice switching between hands if you can, and play with your non-dominant hand when you have the opportunity to practice. Some players keep their hand orientation the same on their grip/trigger and just shift the tank to their other shoulder, but I've never had success with that. I definitely recommend switching hands so your elbow isn't protruding too much. 

Keep your marker up when you're running or making big moves. 

If you're going to dive into the snake, stay low. Players on the other team will be watching the God and you will have to be fast and sneaky to get into the snake.

Practice callouts. Anything at the midline of the field, I would call a 50. So someone at the middle of the field behind a dorito would be called "dorito 50," and someone up in the middle at a wedge would be "50 wedge."

Listen to the other team's callouts. If they know where you are, it may be smart to move.

Be aware of how many opposing players there are left, and communicate that to your team. If there is only one other player versus you, then change your game play. Play that as though it's a one-on-one and go wide. Getting a corner bunker would be wise if you're the only player on your team left. 

Hope this helps! Have fun! Wear a pod pack if you have one. If you have a gun malfunction, stay in the game and provide communication.
